The Gift That Keeps on Giving: What Is Four In A Row?

Picture this: Last Christmas, my 5-year-old nephew Owen tore into a small box wrapped in shiny gold paper. Inside was a laminated four in a row for kids board, a tiny drawstring pouch, and a handful of red and yellow tokens. He just stared at it. Confused. That's it?

Fast-forward twenty minutes. We're on the floor. He's deeply analyzing every move. Cutting me off. Beaming with pride. He beat me. Twice. Want to know the best part? That thin little board became his absolute road-trip hero for three solid years. Cheaper than a screen. Squeezes right into a glovebox. It's a no-brainer.

So, what even is this nostalgic square with the grid of blinking pockets? It's deceptively simple. Two players take turns dropping a colored chip into any vertical slot. Gravity pulls the chip down. The first person lining up quatre-in-a-row – horizontally, vertically, or diagonally – wins. Pure spaghetti-brain beauty designed in the late '70s to make minds fire on all cylinders while you laugh.
